text_fidelity_a:
Speed Brite Turbo Ionic Cleaner 200SB I have an older version of this produced in 2003 that lacks the convenient mesh basket and wall adapter. And, yes, I eBayed it for a steal. But this machine is definitely worth it, especially if you have (a) a lot of jewelry with porous stones, (b) a lot of sterling silver jewelry, or (c) a lot of jewelry and a strong aversion to noxious smells (the sparkle gem concentrate is relatively tame even to my multiple chemical sensitivities nose). I know of no other machine other than a professional jeweler's that can handle these things.

While I wish I could afford a lot of white gold jewelry, I have a lot of silver. Moreover, I'm not the sort of person who throws out a pair of earrings after it tarnishes. I search for what I want and do my best to preserve it. My skin is very sensitive to tarnish, so keeping on top of tarnish is important to me. And getting my hands very black while keeping on top of tarnish is less than ideal. The only downside that I'm sure would be a downside with sonic machines as well is that it may release glued in gems from their bearings. Also my instructions cautioned to only let hematite sit in the solution rather than applying the electrical current to it.

Now you may have noticed that the speed brite company only recommends something like 5 seconds for silver. There is a reason for this. If there is braiding or filigree or other little mechanical parts to your silver, these may either serve as catch alls where tarnish that is being freed accumulates, OR the oxidized bits that had accumulated in them will, if the silver is cleaned in this machine repeatedly, start to wash onto the shiny silver areas and leave brown, black, or purple streaks. Also, if your water is getting dirty, bends in smoother silver may take on some tarnish. That said, I find it useful to do multiple long cleanings on my silver with some special techniques and big caveats:

First off, when continuing on this long-cleaning silver path you do so at your own risk. I learned by trial and error and thought at first that I had ruined two pieces of jewelry until I figured out how to "fix" them. On the other hand, you will get WAY more of the tarnish off with the machine if you do multiple long soaks. One key that I have found invaluable when daring to clean my filigree or braided pieces at length with this machine is moving the hanging bar smoothly but steadily throughout the cleaning. This makes it much less likely that tarnish will stick back on. Indeed, this is important for all heavily tarnished pieces as well. If gripping the actual item with the clip, then varying where you attach the clip is also helpful. Making sure the water with the sparkle gem is on the cleaner side of things when cleaning filigree or braided pieces is also invaluable, as they will be especially susceptible to picking up tarnish already present in the water.

Sometimes I find an item that I want to resurrect from the dead that is throughly black, often with areas that are braided or actually intended to be oxidized. What I do in these cases is swirl constantly, move the clip constantly, and in between cleanings, wipe the smoother parts of the silver design under running water with my thumbs to wash off some of the tarnish. Basically I use the machine just enough on such pieces as to get the smoother parts of silver partially clean and then use a cloth. Also, I only clean these pieces when I am about to dump the water out so as not to ruin the water for other jewelry.

Now the sparkle gem ionic cleaner will not remove ALL of your tarnish, and as far as I know, it does not deposit any anti-tarnish coating on your jewelry. For this I have lately been using the Connoisseur jewelry cloths. However, if you have any plain old lint-free cloths around, it is useful to run the chains and so forth along these first (there will likely be some loose tarnish) as to save your chemical jewelry cloths for the final stage of cleaning. Especially with the very powerful Connoisseur brand, you can go through those cloths like crazy as they find layer after layer of tarnish on stuff that already looked clean.

I hope that helps!
text_fidelity_b: Speed Brite Turbo Ionic Cleaner 200SB

I have been doing the inversion at 45 degrees for a minute or two at a time, two or three times a day. I tried 60 degrees, but 45 is best for me. The table is sturdy overall, thought the leg and foot mechanism is a little shaky (I would not trust it if I were close to the 300 pound limit). It was easy to assemble - you just need to take your time and follow each step of the instructions carefully. There is one step that requires two people.
I am 6 feet tall and about 180 pounds. If I set the adjustable height at 6'2", I get perfect balance.
What I dislike is the head rest. It doesn't matter which setting is used to adjust it, the problem is just that it has a headrest that is thicker then the body. If the goal is to invert and allow pressure to come off the the neck and back, why do I want something forcing my neck to jut forward instead of being freely aligned with my back. If you are thinking of buying this to help with your neck, I would recommend a table that is flat - the neck and back supported at the same level (when horizontal, of course). I have enjoyed the inversion table, and have no problems with it's overall quality. I wish I had purchased a different one, though, due to the headrest.

text_fidelity_a: Sawyer Products SP105 MINI Water Filtration System, Single, Black How can a typical backpacker or survivalist review this?  I cannot analyze water before and after through a chemical analysis.  I have to operate a bit on trust and  on taste.  The technology has been evaluated by labs over the years.  So I have tested these according to a 'taste test.'  I do not taste the water purifying compound our fine municipal service uses for our daily water supply.  Brewed coffee tastes 'just that little bit better' when I filtered the water.  I read that Sawyer products are used in serious 'Third World' situations, so I think we will be 'good to go' in the 'Wilds' of Charlottesville, VA or the Great Smokey Mountains or the Blue Ridge Mountains.  I like the standard 'bottle' neck size on these:  I can swap out the small squeeze bag for a larger, empty energy drink bottle.  The straw option that fits on the filter inflow permits sucking up water from pools in shallow streams.  The set comes with a syringe-style backflow flusher to clean the filter of debris.
text_fidelity_b: Sawyer Products SP105 MINI Water Filtration System, Single, Black

text_fidelity_a: SurviMate Portable Water Filter Pump for Hiking Camping Travel Emergency use with Activated Carbon & 3 Filter Stages I added 4 stars for "flavor" but in reality, if in a situation where you need this filtering pump to get drinkable water, it may not taste like bottled water or even close to tap water.  My reason for getting this water filter was for emergency situations.  Think about recent disasters - hurricanes, tornadoes and fast-spreading fires - where people had to walk away from their homes and while the Red Cross or other agencies work to help all those affected, there may come a time when you will be left on your own to deal with being unable to return to your home right away and no place to go.  If you have a go-bag with some essentials, then at least you have options.  Having this water filter gives you a better chance to subsist for a while on your own.  That's my reasoning for having this item which is now in my go bag and it gives me much greater peace of mind than thinking the federal government is going to be there for me should a natural disaster occur in my area!  I would recommend this to anyone who like to hike in the woods as well as those who are stocking a go-bag.

Due to a cold snap I won't get to try these on the course until next week. Indoors, my first impression was that they are not very bright. Boy was I wrong. I put one (white) on a transparent yellow Teebird and tossed it around in the back yard last night. The light was very bright in the dark. Per the description, I received four white, two red, two green, and two blue. The white lights also seemed to be two white-white (daylight?) and two more yellowish-whites (incandescent-like).

The lights are about 1-1/8" diameter. They have a circular foam seal, however they do not have adhesive. To affix mine, I used clear packing tape. This is indicated in the description, so it was no surprise...just thought I'd call it out anyway. I think the packing tape is much more secure than any self-adhesive strip.

The batteries do not appear to be intended as replaceable. Per the description the secured battery will not fall out or come loose when in use. Time will tell how long they last, but I'm guessing they have plenty of juice for many games.

I'm looking forward to tossing these around next week when it warms up!

text_fidelity_a:
ALPS OutdoorZ Extreme Traverse X WOW! That's the first word that came to my mind when I opened the box this pack was delivered in. The last time I wore any backpack was when I was a Boy Scout--and that was about 55 years ago. I remember thinking what a great backpack that was. Its ability to swallow massive quantities of camping gear and personal items was impressive although there never seemed to be space for enough food to keep a growing 12 year old happy. The later addition of the first rudimentary frame was considered a luxury although comfort took a back seat to utility.

This ALPS OutdoorZ Extreme Traverse X Hunting Pack (whew) is the "Swiss Army Knife" of backpacks, providing enough features to be adaptable for several potential uses. It's a lot like one of those "pop out" RVs that provide additional space by expanding, but only when you need it. Otherwise it's a neat and efficient package. The frame is a molded of structural foam that fits the curve of your back, the wide straps are padded to ease the burden on your shoulders, and expanding the "wings" increases the comfort by keeping the pack stable around your middle. The construction is robust and uses high grade materials for the fabric, zippers, and buckles. A versatile design allows you to tailor its use to your particular needs. The camouflage pattern allows you to fade into the forest/wetlands should you need to make yourself unnoticeable.

Right now I am using this to carry guns, ammunition, water, insect repellent, sunscreen, targets, and various tools to the shooting range. Because I have a bad back, carrying a heavy duffle bag on one side of my body is a recipe for muscle spasms. Instead I can shoulder this pack, carry all of the stuff I need, and not risk hurting myself. Once I have really gotten comfortable with how to stuff as much as possible into this pack, I will start configuring it into my "bug out bag". If/when the SHTF you need to be able to shoulder a pack at a moment's notice with all the practical stuff you need to survive on your own until things cool off. Of course you also need to know that whatever you choose to take with you can be evenly distributed in your pack and that the weight doesn't become a limiting factor.

This pack is strong and versatile enough to be put to many different uses, and you can be comfortable knowing that it's built to last. This isn't just a hunting pack, it's an extremely versatile carry system.
text_fidelity_b: ALPS OutdoorZ Extreme Traverse X

text_fidelity_a:
LEBBOULDER Gym Gloves/Workout Grips: Quality Neoprene Pads for Men & Women’s Weightlifting, Crossfit Training, Fitness or Exercise Unfortunately, these just didn't work for me so I had to send them back. On the plus side, they're surprisingly well made for the cost. I used these regularly for a few weeks, rinsing them off by hand after every workout and throwing them in the washing machine a couple of times, yet they never showed any wear and tear. The padding on the palms was sufficient to prevent callouses from forming, which is the main purpose of hand protection for me for the gym.

Unfortunately, these were just too big. I'm a woman, 5'2", with hands proportional to my height. Other reviews mentioned having extra material on the palms, but I decided to risk trying these anyway since many buyers reported that this wasn't a big deal. That part wasn't a major problem for me either, but the finger loops were way too big. Also, I found that my palms tended to get sweaty while wearing these, though that decreased a bit over time; eventually, I think I would've gotten used to them and not sweated with them on, or at least not so much. Still, the oversized grips plus the tendency for my palms to sweat meant that I couldn't get a good grip, especially when lifting heavy or doing swings. That's why I ultimately returned them.

Although these didn't work for me, I think they could be a good option for those with slightly larger hands. If you're of at least average height, you'd probably be okay with these. And even if you're not, the generous return period means that you have enough time to test these for yourself at no risk. I understand that offering different sizes would likely mean a price increase, but I hope the company is able to do this one day. If they maintained the build quality, a small price increase would still make these grips good value for money, and I'd jump at the chance to buy a slightly smaller version of this product.
text_fidelity_b: LEBBOULDER Gym Gloves/Workout Grips: Quality Neoprene Pads for Men & Women’s Weightlifting, Crossfit Training, Fitness or Exercise

MOON LENCE 2 PCS Body Boards for Beach Lightweight with EPS Core & Wrist Leash 33/37/41" Body Board with Slick Bottom Surfing for Kids Teens and Adults My wife and I love going to the beach and had been wanting body boards for a long time. So when I had the chance, I grabbed these MOON LENCE Body Board - we are thrilled with them! Ok, maybe we’re just big kids at heart, but that’s the way life should be, so riding the waves is a lot of fun and today we spent a couple hours on these boards. From start to finish it was a great time and we can’t wait to go back... except, we are pretty sure this was the last weekend it’ll be warm enough even in our hot weather state, so yea, we wish we’d gotten them earlier, but no worry, we’ll have them for next year (or next weekend with any luck).

They are a great set - two is always better than one when you’ve got two people as you don’t have to share. We went with the yellow because let’s face it, they’re easy to see - they really are! The materials are excellent. The front has a slight texture that feels good - meaning you’re not scratched or feel rough when laying on it - and it lets you have a better grip. We had decent waves today and never once felt like we didn’t not have control. The back is smooth and rides the wave well. It is so well designed and done - compared to others we have looked at and not bought - that we would most certainly look at more in the future from the same line. I”m a bit heavier at present and I was still able to get the waves - though we could not get out as far and I was dropping deeper than my wife so had to watch in the shallower waters. The strap for your wrist was great. My wife put them on - they come unattached - and did mention it’s threading the needle - needs a soft touch, yet easy to do. Once on they STAYED ON! I mean you’d have thought these were pro boards or something they felt, looked, and rode so well. It was a bit of an effort getting the velcro undone the first time - we both ended up pulling from the inside to get it open - but in the end, they stayed secured to us as the waves let us have it. We had a great time today - and as mentioned above, hope we get maybe another weekend out there. Thrilled to have these MOON LENCE Body Boards!

A Mustard Seed Toys Tungsten Putty Weight, 1 oz, Get The Perfect Weights for Your Pinewood Car to Win Your Derby I've been working on pinewood derby cars for a while. I first started with my children, then the past 10 years holding derby car clinics.

Tungsten putty is important to get your car to maximum weight. I keep the unassembled car weighted at 4.9 ounces. I drill a shallow 1/4 hole under the car and pack in the tungsten putty to make up the last bit of weight. That way on race day you can make small weight adjustments without trashing your car. The fastest car is the heaviest.

I've been getting tungsten putty from the large online derby suppliers. I figured I'd save money in shipping, use Amazon prime, and try a new product. This putty is less dense than the putty I've worked with in the past. It seems to have more sticky binder and less tungsten powder than what I've used in the past. I ordered 3 units. They easily fit inside one container. I even mixed some tungsten powder to the 3 blobs of putty.

I prefer the stuff I got before but this will work

FILA Accessories Resistance Band with Handles - Exercise Band Workout Cord with Comfort-Foam Handles for Fitness Strength Training | Ideal for Home Gym, Women, Men We have been working to improve and sustain our fitness, especially as we move through middle age. With a number of items we currently use (hand weights, bench w/weight bar, kettle bells, etc) we were looking at resistance bands to augment our options. We live in an apartment, so while there is the community workout room, in the age of Covid, we are avoiding that space. Two people working out at the same time can also take up too. much room and I sometimes workout late at night and do not want to make noise. So we took a chance on the FILA Accessories Resistance Band with Handles and we come away positive and happy with it.

This band is a great compliment to what we are already doing. I’ve been working on two areas: upper body/arms and lower body/legs/core. This supports that overall goal.

In my experience this heavy resistance has been great for my arms and challenges me. I do feel a solid burn and full on resistance.

My core does feel it unless I focus and make certain I’m getting it involved.
This so far there is little affect on my bottom half/legs. It does include an exercise chart with several options, which does include a lunge. I have not yet done the lunge.

Which brings me to: you must wear shoes!

My first time, as I took it out of the box and wanted to see, I was barefoot. Not smart. NOT that it caused pain.

But it didn’t feel great on the bottom of my feet as I pulled. The rubber band is a rubbery, hard tubing and it pulled on the bottom and was uncomfortable to stand and apply pressure on. I added the shoes and all was well.

Overall I think this is a great product and we are happy with it.

I will say there is a limit: it is Heavy Resistance and no way to interchange with others resistance levels. Other packages come with multiple resistance options. But if you are looking for a single weight, this does the trick.

We were also discussing how this would be great for travel. Again, with Covid, rather than worry about taking heavy hand weights or kettle bells or use a hotel’s workout space, this would be far easier and lighter. So that will be the plan for the future.

One Con: the handles are not the most comfortable. This is not enough to keep me from using the band. They are rough I’m sure in order to assure grip, but in future I’ll use weight gloves to get a better grip and counter the uncomfortable feeling of these.

Overall we are pleased with this Resistance Band and foresee continued successful use.
text_fidelity_b: FILA Accessories Resistance Band with Handles - Exercise Band Workout Cord with Comfort-Foam Handles for Fitness Strength Training | Ideal for Home Gym, Women, Men

Electric Foot Warmer for Men and Women with Non-Slip，Fast Heating Pad with Four Layer Temperature Locking System,Foot Warmer Under Desk.Electric Foot Heating pad with 3 Temperature Settings. The foot warmer seems to be made of good quality fabric and leather.

The foot warmer has three temperature settings: 38C (100F), 42C (108F), and 55C (131F). When I turned the foot warmer on at room temperature, it listed 22C. I adjusted the temperature to the hottest setting of 55C. I kept it going for 45 minutes, with both my feet in the warmer. After 20 minutes or so the warmer stabilized at a temperature of 43 to 44C. 25 minutes later, the temperature had not changed, never reaching anywhere close to 55C. 44C was warm enough, but not what was promised.

Besides the temperature limit, two drawbacks for me (may not apply to other people):
- The foot warmer has USB-C input, and it comes with a USB-A to USB-C cable. Note that the warmer only accepts 10W, and if you try to use a USB-C to USB-C cable that delivers higher wattage, the foot warmer will not work. Ideally the foot warmer's electronics would be designed to take as much wattage as they need, and no more, in the same way I can connect an iphone and an ipad pro to the same fast-charging brick, and each device would accept only as much wattage as appropriate, instead of burning out or shutting down.
- This foot warmer seems to be designed for those who shoe sizes 11 and under. I wear size 13 shoes, and my feet barely fit, with my toes partially curled. Pretty uncomfortable. The product description makes no reference to foot size, and unfortunately for me, I cannot use this foot warmer effectively. Otherwise, it does its job well.
text_fidelity_b: Electric Foot Warmer for Men and Women with Non-Slip，Fast Heating Pad with Four Layer Temperature Locking System,Foot Warmer Under Desk.Electric Foot Heating pad with 3 Temperature Settings.

text_fidelity_a:
Eberlestock Phantom Pack This is far and away the finest pack I've ever used. Basically a Halftrack with the addition of a removable scabbard.
Quality of construction is top notch pretty much everywhere. That's a good thing, because there are zippers in several key areas, which I consider a strategic weakness. The scabbard zips to the main ruck, with spring clips at the top. The zippers each have a little hook that they catch on to keep them from accidentally riding up and the scabbard coming loose -- very nicely done. The handles are very sturdy, and well placed. PALS webbing is very useful, and well placed. I have several pouches of assorted types in various places. I'm extremely happy with this pack.

Minor beefs:
-The shoulder straps are far apart, designed for guys with a large frame. I'm a bit on the small side, and it's uncomfortable if I don't have the front clip pulled tight to keep the shoulder straps closer together.
-The belt only attaches to the scabbard, and without the scabbard it's shoulder straps only.
-the bottom of the scabbard hangs down without a reliable means of pulling it up out of the way when not in use. I've tried folding mine up, but it doesn't stay. Not a big deal, but it should have some sort of hook or clip like the Scabbard's zippers do.
-Zippers form the critical connectors in several points, with no backup if they fail. Granted, these are some tough zippers, but I've seen tough zippers fail before. I have a half dozen very nice, heavy duty packs with zippers that have failed. I like the utility of the zipper, but it needs some contact points for a backup -- even just putting PALS webbing all along the zipper surfaces would allow field expedient 550 cord securement, though you could argue that the addition of such potential snag points increases the likelihood of zipper failure due to catastrophic hang-ups.
text_fidelity_b: Eberlestock Phantom Pack

text_fidelity_a:
StoreYourBoard Replacement 12 Inch Balloon Wheels Kayak Dolly and Sand Carts, Big Beach Buggy Inflatable Tires We loved the Rio Wonder Wheeler concept, but it didn't work so great in practice. When loaded, it was very difficult to pull over the sand. We then looked at higher-priced ones with balloon wheels, knowing that those would work better on soft sand. I convinced my husband to try these wheels on the Wonder Wheeler first. We followed the advice of other reviewers and bought a 36" length - 3/8" diameter steel rod from ACE (couldn't find one at Home Depot) and 4 metal flat washers to fit the rod (which would be used as new axle). We drilled a hole 1/2 inch from both ends using a titanium drill bit (the carbide one we bought was useless). We used 1/2" pvc pipe cut to the width of the new wheels. We inflated the tires to 4 lbs. with an electric pump; removed linch pins from original axle (don't lose these or plastic bushings), removed original big plastic wheels, bushings, and axle.
To assemble with new tires: 1) We inserted new axle; 2) then the original bushings (with end protrusion cut off); 3) then a metal washer; 4) new tire with pvc inserted through center; 5) another washer; and 6) inserted original linch pins through drilled holes (repeat steps 2-6 on other side). It now works like a dream and saved us several hundred dollars since we didn't have to buy a new cart.
text_fidelity_b: StoreYourBoard Replacement 12 Inch Balloon Wheels Kayak Dolly and Sand Carts, Big Beach Buggy Inflatable Tires

text_fidelity_a:
Trek Tents 10 x 14' Canvas Cabin Tent Khaki Yes, it Does work. Tension is the key.
Looking at the pictures of this tent you can see that it Should work, but you Doubt it, right??
Here on the NorthCoast of California right next to that big body of water, we have normal breezes running around 15 mph. When it gets a bit Windy it'll run around 35 mph. Then there's when it gets brisk ;>
It's still hanging out in the place I'd staked it when other tents had hopped the fence and wandered down the street.
I'd gotten tired of having to replace those nylon things every year or two and wanted something a lot more permanent in a temporary structure.
The canvas is IT for me!
I like that they'd used a white for the roofing giving you a more open feeling than you'd have otherwise if they'd gone with the base color.
I'm very happy with the construction. Tabs, zipper-pulls, netting in doors and windows. The floor is sturdy enough to dance on.
The tie-downs and stakes need to be replaced. I'm really very disappointed that this tent has such a poor finish after all the fine work they'd done for the main structure.
The skinny and very stretchy nylon strings and skinny smooth metal pins they give you stretch when dampened and the pegs pull out. It's an easy fix, not to worry. Just get a length of REAL Rope and re-do the tie-downs and buy a handful of those lovely orange plastic pegs that have teeths and you'll Keep the proper tension in the roof you need for when you get 3 inches of rain dumped on you, even With the rain-fly covering the roof. You will of course need to re-adjust the tie-downs after this happens. Good News!! Even with a couple of tub fulls of rain on the tent that you'll need to dump off, the tent Remains STANDING!

UPDATE:
After the ground got SUPER saturated with days of rain and some SERIOUS winds and GUSTS, it's collapsed Twice and the rain fly has completely died. The tie down banding along one edge RIPPED OFF and the ties From the tent to the Center pole ripped off.
The rain fly needs to be anchored SEPARATELY if you also have issue with winds. Since it's integrated with the tent, it causes Severe wall flapping and even with heavy duty metal tent pegs doing their Best, it still collapses.
NOT A HAPPY CAMPER :(((
2ND UPDATE:
We have some fairly Serious WIND and RAIN issues here and this tent does NOT hold up. The first thing that went was the rain fly, as you might have noted from my First post.
I'd replaced the useless tie down strings that came with and got some screw in the ground pegs to hold the metal framing, also noted above.
Now, the loops are ripping out.

text_fidelity_a:
ANOOPSYCHE Bodyweight Fitness Resistance Trainer Kit with Body Workout Guide, Fitness Training Straps for Home or Professional Complete Body Workout Seems to be a good quality piece of workout equipment. Nice and versatile. The web strapping is a good thickness. Surprising how heavy it was in the box. I have a similar product from Golds Gym. This one from Anoopsyche is thicker and heavier.

Perhaps my favorite thing about this product is that the two handles are separate, which makes doing exercises (pushing, pulling, and foot in strap) much more comfortable than with one that is connected at the top.

A close second is the versatility in setting it up. It'll wrap around a bar or wedge in a closed door.

It also includes a strap that connects both sides to one mounting spot. Honestly, I'm not sure why. It's plenty long separated. Combined I think that it would be overly long unless your mounting to an extra high mounting spot. You could probably mount this thing ten foot off the ground with the additional strap without a problem. Personally, the handle sections alone are enough for me.

The buckles seem to be good quality buckles.

Deducting one star for quality control. The two handle straps are different lengths. Which is a mute point because the straps are adjustable. Just causes me to have to double check that I've adjusted both straps to equal lengths. You figure out pretty quick when both hands are in different positions because of different lengths. I ordered a second set at the same time for a friend. I opened that box to check the length of the straps. In that box both straps were the same length. I'll continue using the odd length ones and give the friend the even length ones for their convenience.
text_fidelity_b: ANOOPSYCHE Bodyweight Fitness Resistance Trainer Kit with Body Workout Guide, Fitness Training Straps for Home or Professional Complete Body Workout

text_fidelity_a:
Champion Traps and Targets .22 Bullet Trap (Rimfire Only) I'd been wanting to teach my youngest daughter the basics of gun safety and help her get comfortable firing a weapon. However, I didn't want to take her to a gun range with its attendant loud noises and general confusion. I only wanted her to concentrate on the weapons and on what I had to tell her. We live in a neighborhood where the homes each sit on 2.5 acre lots--and most of them have surrounding fencing. While I could have set up a target range in our basement, I didn't want to deal with lead and gunpowder, and I also wanted to be able to push the boundaries to make her comfortable and capable with a rifle.

So I bought this trap and mounted it on two heavy duty pallets, put two more tall pallets behind it, and hung some heavy cardboard behind the target in the trap. Behind the pallets are some mounds of fill dirt and 100 feet of thick brush. In addition, there are no neighbors behind us for over two miles. The heavy cardboard was to stop any bullet splash back and also to help lower the sound of the bullet hitting the trap.

The final key to keeping all this a secret was to use two legal suppressors I have on the semi autos. You can use a variety of ammunition in both the rifle and pistol without having to deal with the "crack" of the bullets, giving you the opportunity to match each gun with the best ammo for it. And no one is the wiser. Mission accomplished!
text_fidelity_b: Champion Traps and Targets .22 Bullet Trap (Rimfire Only)

text_fidelity_a:
Workout Logbook for Women & Men; Mother's Day Gift; 90 Day Fitness Planner & Tracker; Journal; Gym Journal; Gym Logbook; Fitness Diary; Exercise Journal; Gift for Athletes; Athletes's Journal Following a few injuries my wife and I are getting back to our workouts, but wanted to get some bigger steps this time and specific outcomes, so we decided to grab some journals. I had gotten one that leans on more of a weight-centric program. My wife is more mixed between cardio and weights, so I thought this one might be of help. In the end, this is an okay, not good nor great journal, but will do something to at least let her track. She will use it, but we agree, it is not the best option for anyone beyond a beginner starting out.

1. It is made from decent materials with a hard cardboard front and back to give stability when working inside. The binding is spiral, allowing it to fully open and not bunch up the pages. From this aspect, it is well done.

2. The options within are more limited than mine and others we have looked at.

A. The introduction of Why is pretty basic, but good for beginners, but limited for those beyond.

B. There are places to track your weight and body shape changes at the beginning, 30 day, 60 day, and 90 day marks. There are no spots for doing so between, which in my expense and from my reading, one should not track weight and other elements daily. Some suggest weekly or monthly. In this case, it is monthly (every 30 days). My journal offers weekly tracking with more options on WHAT to track and HOW to do it. I think this is notable in that while mine and this Training Journal; Fitness Journal; Fitness Planner and Tracker tracks the same elements of the body, mine provides little diagrams of WHERE on the body these points lie. As I think this Training Journal; Fitness Journal; Fitness Planner and Tracker is lacking this information, which if geared towards beginners, would be helpful information.

C. My journal offers far more options on all of these aspects across the board. For example, mine has space for 13 exercises per page and Sets 1 - 6 whereas this Training Journal; Fitness Journal; Fitness Planner and Tracker has it strangely set up in Sets 1 - 5 with Weight and Reps. It's as if they see a Set as an exercise and think you are doing five exercises. At least that's how we are reading it. Then you put in how many reps. in each set.

D. Things like Water intake in this Training Journal; Fitness Journal; Fitness Planner and Tracker are just a question: Water Intake? In mine (and others) they tend to have a way to track, such as something open you fill in when you have a glass or something you check off. I prefer such a way in that you tick it off with each one as opposed to this Training Journal; Fitness Journal; Fitness Planner and Tracker which is answering a question - "5." Now you're having to keep track to fill it out. YES, you can certainly check off or make tick marks - but that really should be set up in the design.

E. Little things like tracking what area of the body or muscles you worked (legs, core, back, etc) are NOT included here which is a shame. But they do include things like "Next session modifications and/focus"... not even sure what that would mean - I THINK it's their way of having you in fact track if you did core, legs, chest, etc. The space available for these question answers is pretty limited.

F. Another reviewer noted there are "Examples" provided in some pages but are printed on the lines and you have to write over it. It is true how they printed it and it's kind of annoying. Why would I want to keep writing over it?

G. While not as bad in the wording and grammar of many products made in China, there are some obvious (glaring) strange parts. Nothing one cannot workout and that make this a bad book, but they are notable.

In the end, this Training Journal; Fitness Journal; Fitness Planner and Tracker is okay and would be fine for many beginners looking to workout and track that journey for the first 90 days. It is not in your face, it is a way to learn and pace yourself and and get the information down. I don't think it's all that bad that it would be with a 1 or 2 star rating, but certainly does not earn 4 or 5. In the end I went with 3 because it is workable, easy to use and write in, and it does provide elements one wishes to track when getting into a practice. That said, there are much better options on the market, even for beginners, and I would personally look elsewhere.
text_fidelity_b: Workout Logbook for Women & Men; Mother's Day Gift; 90 Day Fitness Planner & Tracker; Journal; Gym Journal; Gym Logbook; Fitness Diary; Exercise Journal; Gift for Athletes; Athletes's Journal

text_fidelity_a:
Callaway Men's Mack Daddy 2 Wedge (Slate Finish, Custom Sole C-Grind) Being a lifetime hacker (22 hcp), I was reluctant to spend a lot of money on a wedge, but I was in need of one desperately. My short game is usually my downfall so I researched and found the Callaway Mack Daddy 2. I chose to go with the 60 degree "C" grind due to the fact that I love to hit flop shots as well as standard chips, pitches, approaches, etc. Check out the videos on callaway's website for more info on which grind is best for you.

The wedge comes in a matte chrome or slate finish. I chose to go with the slate finish as I liked the darker look and thought I would like the oxidation look as well. Looking back I think I would likely have chosen the chrome finish as it requires less maintenance. The slate finish will rust and require you to scrub off the rust as time goes by. Callaway recommends you keep a small patch of Scotch-Brite Purple in your bag for scrubbing it off. A lubricant cleaner can also be used to help keep the rust off the finish.

The handling of this wedge is amazing. As I said, my short game has sucked, partly because I haven't put enough time in and partly because my wedge always was a hand-me-down. After getting this wedge and practicing with it quite a bit I'm in love. I usually use hard covered balls because I hate losing a nice soft covered ball. Even with using a hard covered ball I'm able to get some pretty good backspin on the ball when pitching or approaching the green. Flop shots are incredibly easy with this wedge thanks to the "C" grind and I've improved nearly every aspect of my short game in part to this club.

The groves are the highest degree allowed by the USGA and the laser etched pattern really helps put extra spin on the ball.

Overall I love this club immensely. It gives you great control of the ball with whatever shot you are trying to hit. I'm planning on picking up a 52 or 54 degree wedge as well, in the future. Excellent club, can't recommend it enough!
text_fidelity_b: Callaway Men's Mack Daddy 2 Wedge (Slate Finish, Custom Sole C-Grind)

text_fidelity_a:
NiteRider Commuter Helmet Mount F/Cordless & Mako Got this to mount a MiNewt 150 on my helmet, and it's working well so far. It's kind of a tie-down thing with some pipe-insulation-like rubber under the plastic foot/pedestal to keep it from sliding around on the helmet. I've had it for about 2-3 weeks, so I can't comment on durability, but it has the same quick-release setup as the handlebar mount packaged with the 150. It tilts front and back, though not side-to-side. I'm using it with a Bell road helmet, and had no problems mounting it right in the center--as long as you have symmetrical vents in your helmet, you should be ok.

Good Stuff
With the right adjustments, you can get a good view of what's (well) ahead of you, and having it helmet-mounted allows you to pan and sweep the road ahead for pointy stuff and potholes. I also use it to alert drivers when approaching intersections--a quick look left and right gives a flash in their direction to get attention. The on-helmet setup seems to allow for longer "reach" from the light as well. One added bonus--drivers of high-profile vehicles (monster trucks, etc.) are more likely to see you since the light is well above the handlebars.

Notes and Concerns
If going for long rides in the dark, I'd recommend keeping a small blinky on the handlebars to complement the helmet mount (if you're not looking straight-ahead, your light isn't either). The mount is also made mainly of plastic--not sure what that does for long-term durability--may want to take it off if not doing night/dark rides, to minimize UV damage in the sun, etc. The mount does make the light sit rather high on the head, so it's not going to improve your aerodynamics or get you any style points (like a Roman centurion helmet profile), and it of course adds a bit of weight to the helmet.

Overall
I'd recommend this, especially for anyone who rides in the dark frequently or for long periods of time.
text_fidelity_b: NiteRider Commuter Helmet Mount F/Cordless & Mako

Honestly. . . I don't know a lot about "lumens". . . but I just know that this thing is BRIGHT. When it says that it's a "focusing" flashlight, that means you can put a spotlight one sometime. If you're holding it out, then depending upon how coordinated you are, you might have to use two hands to turn it off.

This flashlight is an investment. It's not something you're going to get at the 99 cent store. But it should last you a very long time.
